content:
Jin dragged his aching body through the wet brambles, his bare toes turning purple against the ice-crusted loam. He knelt by the spring and plunged his face straight into the freezing mud, drinking deeply of the raw mineral runoff. 

Sitting cross-legged on a flat granite slab, he closed his eyes and forced his breath into the ancient four-stroke cadence of the Mount Hua Morning Dew Art. He drew ambient atmospheric Qi through the crown of his skull, funneling it down toward his dantian.

*CRACKLE.*

The biological resistance was agonizing. His twelve primary meridians were clogged with decades of mineral silt and cellular debris, calcified like rusted lead pipes. The Qi caught against the blockage; blood welled in his nostrils and spattered across the frost.
critique: Sanderson: Strong biological limits and mechanical vector precision.
